blocks.heading: Production and productivity
blocks.text: Production is the activity of creating goods or services to meet needs. Productivity relates output to an input, such as acceptable units per labour hour. More total output is not necessarily higher productivity if inputs rise faster. State the input and time period and compare like quality. A larger staff producing more items can still produce fewer items per worker. Product is the offering; production is making it; productivity measures how efficiently the stated input generates output.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Tula Packs makes 400 packs with ten workers in one week and later 480 with twelve workers working equal hours. Output rises, but output per worker remains forty packs in each period. That is increased production without improved labour productivity under the stated comparable hours.

blocks.heading: Production
blocks.text: Production is creating goods or services from inputs to satisfy needs. It can involve manufacturing, farming or service activity and is not restricted to a factory making objects. A production total records output over a period, while productivity relates output to input. The distinction matters when judging whether extra resources are used more efficiently.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Eya Repairs completes more repairs after hiring another technician. The service output has increased. Productivity requires comparing repairs with technician time, not merely counting the extra repairs.

blocks.heading: Productivity
blocks.text: Productivity is output per unit of input, such as acceptable products per labour hour. Higher productivity means more output from a given input or the same output with less input, using comparable quality and periods. It differs from production, the activity or total output. A busier workplace can have unchanged or lower productivity if resources rise as quickly as output.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Kena Packs makes 200 packs in 40 labour hours. Labour productivity is five packs per labour hour. More hours alone would not establish an improvement in this rate.
